jelet-2024-q001.conceptSummary: For orthogonal $A$, $B$: $A + B = A(B^{T} + A^{T})B$, so $\det(A+B) = \det A\,\det B\,\det(A+B)$; with $\det A\det B = -1$ this forces $\det(A+B) = 0$.

steps.title: Use orthogonality
steps.bodyLatex: $A^{T}A = I$ and $BB^{T} = I$, hence $A(A^{T} + B^{T})B = (AA^{T})B + A(B^{T}B) = B + A$. So $A + B = A\,(A + B)^{T}\,B$.

steps.title: Take determinants
steps.bodyLatex: $\det(A + B) = \det A \cdot \det\big((A+B)^{T}\big) \cdot \det B = \det A\,\det B\,\det(A+B)$. Orthogonal matrices have $\det = \pm 1$, and $\det A + \det B = 0$ gives $\det A = -\det B$, so $\det A\,\det B = -1$.

steps.title: Solve
steps.bodyLatex: $\det(A+B) = -\det(A+B) \Rightarrow \det(A+B) = 0$, so $A + B$ is singular and $(A+B)^{-1}$ does not exist (D false).

steps.title: Reject (B) and (C)
steps.bodyLatex: Take $A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$ (rotation, $\det = 1$) and $B = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$ (reflection, $\det = -1$): $A + B = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$ is neither symmetric nor orthogonal.

verification.note: SymPy: det(R(t) + F(s)) = 0 identically for every rotation R(t) and reflection F(s); counter-example shows (B), (C) fail.

jelet-2024-q002.conceptSummary: $\det A = 0$ but a $2\times2$ minor is non-zero, so $\operatorname{rank} A = 2$.

steps.title: Determinant
steps.bodyLatex: Expand along column 2 (only the $-1$ is non-zero): $\det A = (-1)\cdot(-1)^{2+2}\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 6 \end{vmatrix} = -(6 - 6) = 0$. So $\operatorname{rank} A < 3$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: $\operatorname{rank} A = 2$. (Row 3 is $2\times$ row 1 in columns 1 and 3, which is why the determinant vanishes.) Answer: (C).

jelet-2024-q003.conceptSummary: $A = I + N$ with $N^{2} = 0$, so $A^{K} = I + KN$.

steps.title: Binomial expansion
steps.bodyLatex: $I$ commutes with $N$, so $A^{K} = (I + N)^{K} = I + KN + \binom{K}{2}N^{2} + \dots = I + KN$.

steps.title: Write out
steps.bodyLatex:
$A^{K} =  egin{pmatrix} 1 + 2K & -4K \ K & 1 - 2K \end{pmatrix}$. Check $K = 1$: $ egin{pmatrix} 3 & -4 \ 1 & -1 \end{pmatrix} = A$. Options (B), (C), (D) already fail at $K = 1$ (entries $1-3K = -2 
eq -1$, $K^{2}$ version gives $1+K^{2} = 2 
eq 3$, $D = I 
eq A$).

verification.note: SymPy: (A - I)^2 = 0 and A^K equals option A for K = 1..8; options B, C, D differ at K = 1.

jelet-2024-q004.conceptSummary: The constant term $t$ of a polynomial identity is its value at $\lambda = 0$.

verification.note: SymPy: the full determinant expands to a quartic in lambda whose constant term is 21.

jelet-2024-q005.conceptSummary: Differentiate a determinant row by row; each derivative row gives a $2\times2$ determinant equal to $\Delta_{2}$.

verification.note: SymPy: diff(det(D1), x) - 3*det(D2) simplifies to 0; options A, C, D are not identities.

jelet-2024-q006.conceptSummary: Take $a$, $b$, $c$ out of the columns, then simplify by row operations.

steps.title: Factor the columns
steps.bodyLatex: Column 1 has factor $a$, column 2 factor $b$, column 3 factor $c$: $\Delta = abc\begin{vmatrix} a & c & a+c \\ a+b & b & a \\ b & b+c & c \end{vmatrix}$.

steps.title: Row operation
steps.bodyLatex: $R_{1} \to R_{1} - R_{2} - R_{3}$: $R_{1} = (-2b,\; -2b,\; 0)$, so $\Delta = -2b\cdot abc\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 0 \\ a+b & b & a \\ b & b+c & c \end{vmatrix}$.

steps.title: Expand
steps.bodyLatex: $\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 0 \\ a+b & b & a \\ b & b+c & c \end{vmatrix} = (bc - a(b+c)) - ((a+b)c - ab) = -2ac$. Hence $\Delta = -2b\cdot abc\cdot(-2ac) = 4a^{2}b^{2}c^{2}$.

verification.note: SymPy: factor(det) = 4*a**2*b**2*c**2.

jelet-2024-q007.conceptSummary: Write both terms in Euler form; $w + 1/w = 2\cos\alpha$ for $w = e^{i\alpha}$.

steps.title: Reject the others
steps.bodyLatex: (A) swaps the angles, (C) and (D) use a single angle; e.g. $m = 1$, $n = 0$, $\theta = \pi/3$, $\phi = 0$ gives the value $2\cos\frac{\pi}{3} = 1$, while (A) gives $2\cos 0 = 2$ and (D) gives $2$.

verification.note: SymPy: the expression equals 2cos(m*theta - n*phi) at random integer m, n and real angles; only option B matches every sample.

jelet-2024-q008.conceptSummary: $w$ is purely imaginary iff $\operatorname{Re} w = 0$; clear the denominator with the conjugate.

steps.title: Real part
steps.bodyLatex: Numerator real part: $x(x - 1) + y(y - 1) = x^{2} + y^{2} - x - y$.

steps.title: Locus
steps.bodyLatex: $\operatorname{Re} = 0 \iff x^{2} + y^{2} - x - y = 0$, i.e. $\left(x - \tfrac12\right)^{2} + \left(y - \tfrac12\right)^{2} = \tfrac12$ (with $Z \neq 1$): equal $x^{2}$, $y^{2}$ coefficients and no $xy$ term.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: The point lies on a circle of centre $\left(\tfrac12, \tfrac12\right)$, radius $\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$. Answer: (B).

verification.note: SymPy: Re((Z-i)/(Z-1)) numerator = x^2 + y^2 - x - y; conic with A = C, B = 0 → circle.

jelet-2024-q009.conceptSummary: Slope of the normal at $t_{1}$ equals the slope of the chord joining $t_{1}$ and $t_{2}$.

steps.title: Tangent slope
steps.bodyLatex: $xy = e^{2} \Rightarrow y' = -\dfrac{y}{x}$. At $\left(et_{1}, \frac{e}{t_{1}}\right)$: $y' = -\dfrac{1}{t_{1}^{2}}$, so the normal has slope $t_{1}^{2}$.

steps.title: Equate
steps.bodyLatex: $t_{1}^{2} = -\dfrac{1}{t_{1}t_{2}} \Rightarrow t_{1}^{3}t_{2} = -1$. Then $t_{1}t_{2} = -1/t_{1}^{2}$, so $(t_{1}t_{2})^{2} = 1/t_{1}^{4}$, which is not $\pm1$ in general: (A), (D) fail, and (C) has the wrong sign.

verification.note: SymPy: solving the normal line with the curve gives t2 = -1/t1^3, so t1^3*t2 = -1 identically.

jelet-2024-q010.conceptSummary: The square of a tangent length from $P$ to $S' = 0$ is $S'(P)$; on the first circle $S(P) = 0$.

steps.title: Power of the point
steps.bodyLatex: For $P(h, k)$ the tangent length to $S'(x,y) = x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c'$ is $\sqrt{S'(h,k)}$.

steps.title: Length
steps.bodyLatex: Length $= \sqrt{c' - c} = (c' - c)^{\frac12}$, the same for every $P$ (the circles are concentric, with $c' < c$ so the second is inside). (A) has no square root, (C) has the wrong sign under the root, (D) $= |c - c'|$.

verification.note: SymPy: with P = (-g + r cos t, -f + r sin t), r^2 = g^2 + f^2 - c, S'(P) simplifies to c' - c.

jelet-2024-q011.conceptSummary: Square both sides: $|\vec A + \vec B|^{2} - |\vec A - \vec B|^{2} = 4\,\vec A\cdot\vec B$.

steps.title: Square
steps.bodyLatex: $|\vec A|^{2} + 2\vec A\cdot\vec B + |\vec B|^{2} = |\vec A|^{2} - 2\vec A\cdot\vec B + |\vec B|^{2}$.

steps.title: Simplify
steps.bodyLatex: $4\,\vec A\cdot\vec B = 0 \Rightarrow |\vec A||\vec B|\cos\theta = 0 \Rightarrow \cos\theta = 0$ for non-zero vectors.

verification.note: SymPy: |A+B|^2 - |A-B|^2 = 4 A.B; solve(cos(theta) = 0) on [0, pi] = pi/2.

steps.title: Square the sum
steps.bodyLatex: $0 = |\vec a + \vec b + \vec c|^{2} = |\vec a|^{2} + |\vec b|^{2} + |\vec c|^{2} + 2(\vec a\cdot\vec b + \vec b\cdot\vec c + \vec c\cdot\vec a)$.

verification.note: SymPy: an explicit planar triangle with sides 3, 4, 2 gives a.b + b.c + c.a = -29/2.

steps.title: Resultant force
steps.bodyLatex: $\vec F = (4\hat i + \hat j - 3\hat k) + (3\hat i + \hat j - \hat k) = 7\hat i + 2\hat j - 4\hat k$.

steps.title: Displacement
steps.bodyLatex: $\vec d = (5\hat i + 4\hat j + \hat k) - (\hat i + 2\hat j + 3\hat k) = 4\hat i + 2\hat j - 2\hat k$.

jelet-2024-q014.conceptSummary: $\sin^{-1}u$ needs $-1 \le u \le 1$; $\log_{2}$ needs a positive argument.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Domain $= [-2, -1] \cup [1, 2]$. (B), (C), (D) cut off part of it at $\sqrt2$. Answer: (A).

verification.note: SymPy: solve_univariate_inequality for -1 <= log(x^2/2, 2) <= 1 gives Union([-2,-1],[1,2]).

jelet-2024-q015.conceptSummary: Split the symmetric difference into a forward and a backward difference quotient.

steps.title: Take the limit
steps.bodyLatex: Both quotients tend to $f'(a)$ as $h \to 0$ because $f'(a)$ exists.

verification.note: SymPy: the limit equals 2f'(a) for test functions sin, exp, x^3, log(1+x) at several points; options A, B, D do not.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: $f(\pi) = 0$. (A) $7$ and (B) $\tfrac72$ come from forgetting the extra factor $t$. Answer: (D).

verification.note: SymPy: limit((1 - cos(7*(x - pi)))/(x - pi), x, pi) = 0.

jelet-2024-q017.conceptSummary: Lagrange's mean value theorem: $f(x) - f(a) = f'(\xi)(x - a) = 0$.

steps.title: Apply the MVT on $[a, x]$
steps.bodyLatex: For any $x \in (a, b]$, $f$ is continuous on $[a, x]$ and differentiable on $(a, x)$, so $f(x) - f(a) = f'(\xi)(x - a)$ for some $\xi \in (a, x)$.

steps.title: Use $f' = 0$
steps.bodyLatex: $f'(\xi) = 0 \Rightarrow f(x) = f(a)$ for all $x \in [a, b]$: $f$ is constant.

steps.title: Reject the others
steps.bodyLatex: $f(x) = 5$ on $[1, 2]$ satisfies the hypotheses but is not $kx$ or $kx^{2}$ for any constant $k$, so (A), (C) are not forced, and (D) is false because (B) holds.

verification.note: SymPy: f = 5 has f' = 0; kx = 5 and kx^2 = 5 have no constant solution k on [1, 2].

steps.title: Check the options
steps.bodyLatex: (A) and (C) include points outside the domain $x > 2$; (D) includes $(3, 4)$ where $f' < 0$.

verification.note: SymPy: solve_univariate_inequality(f'(x) > 0) intersected with x > 2 = Interval.open(2, 3).

jelet-2024-q019.conceptSummary: Substitute the constraint and maximise a downward parabola (or use AM–GM).

steps.title: Stationary point
steps.bodyLatex: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{5x - 3x^{2}}{4}\right) = \dfrac{5 - 6x}{4} = 0 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac56$, $y = \dfrac58$; the second derivative $-\tfrac32 < 0$ gives a maximum.

verification.note: SymPy: maximum of x(5 - 3x)/4 is 25/48 at x = 5/6.

jelet-2024-q020.conceptSummary: $\tan u$ is homogeneous of degree $2$, so Euler's theorem applies to $\tan u$, not $u$.

steps.title: Homogeneity
steps.bodyLatex: $z = \tan u = \dfrac{x^{3} + y^{3}}{x - y}$ satisfies $z(tx, ty) = t^{2}z(x,y)$, so $xz_{x} + yz_{y} = 2z$.

verification.note: SymPy: x*u_x + y*u_y - sin(2u) simplifies to 0 for u = atan((x^3+y^3)/(x-y)); B, C, D are non-zero at sample points.

steps.title: Factor
steps.bodyLatex: Numerator $= 3(x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} - xy - yz - zx)$; denominator $= (x+y+z)(x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} - xy - yz - zx)$.

verification.note: SymPy: simplify(u_x + u_y + u_z) = 3/(x + y + z).

jelet-2024-q022.conceptSummary: The integrand is even: $\int_{-1}^{1} = 2\int_{0}^{1}$, where $|x| = x$.

verification.note: SymPy: integrate(Abs(x) + exp(Abs(x)), (x, -1, 1)) = 2e - 1.

jelet-2024-q023.conceptSummary: Simplify the integrand to $\tfrac12\sin 4x$ using double-angle identities.

verification.note: SymPy: simplify(integrand - sin(4x)/2) = 0 and d/dx(-cos(4x)/8) equals the integrand.

jelet-2024-q024.conceptSummary: King's property: replacing $x$ by $\frac{\pi}{2} - x$ turns $\tan^{3}x$ into $\cot^{3}x$.

verification.note: SymPy: 1/(1+tan^3 x) + 1/(1+tan^3(pi/2 - x)) simplifies to 1; numerical quadrature gives 0.785398... = pi/4.

jelet-2024-q025.conceptSummary: The first-quadrant area of $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}} + \frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}} = 1$ is a quarter of $\pi ab$.

steps.title: Integrate
steps.bodyLatex: $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{4}\sqrt{16 - x^{2}}\,dx$ is a quarter circle of radius $4$, $= 4\pi$; so area $= \dfrac34\cdot4\pi = 3\pi$.

verification.note: SymPy: integrate(3/4*sqrt(16 - x^2), (x, 0, 4)) = 3*pi.

jelet-2024-q026.conceptSummary: Linear ODE $y' + \frac{2}{x}y = \frac{\sin x}{x^{2}}$ with integrating factor $x^{2}$.

steps.title: Check the other options
steps.bodyLatex: (A), (C), (D) also pass through $\left(\frac{\pi}{2}, 1\right)$, but implicit differentiation gives slopes $-\frac{\sin x}{x^{2}} - \frac{2y}{x}$, $\frac{\cos x}{x^{2}} - \frac{2y}{x}$, $-\frac{\cos x}{x^{2}} - \frac{2y}{x}$, none of which is the given slope.

verification.note: SymPy: dsolve gives x^2 y = C - cos x with C = pi^2/4; only option B satisfies both the ODE and the point.

jelet-2024-q027.conceptSummary: Cauchy–Euler: with $x = e^{t}$, $x\,y' = \dot y$ and $x^{2}y'' = \ddot y - \dot y$.

steps.title: Derivatives
steps.bodyLatex: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = e^{-t}\dot y$, $\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = e^{-2t}(\ddot y - \dot y)$; hence $x\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dot y$ and $x^{2}\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}} = \ddot y - \dot y$.

steps.title: Substitute
steps.bodyLatex: $(\ddot y - \dot y) - 2\dot y + 2y = e^{3t} \Rightarrow \ddot y - 3\dot y + 2y = e^{3t}$.

steps.title: Read off
steps.bodyLatex: $a = 1$, $b = -3$, $c = 2$. (B) is the negative of the left side but the right side $e^{3t}$ is fixed, so it is not equivalent.

verification.note: SymPy: with y(x) = Y(log x), x^2 y'' - 2x y' + 2y becomes Y'' - 3Y' + 2Y and x^3 becomes e^{3t}.

steps.title: Classify
steps.bodyLatex: Equal coefficients of $x^{2}$ and $y^{2}$ and no $xy$ term: a circle of radius $5$ centred at the origin.

verification.note: SymPy: x^2 + y^2 = 25 satisfies dy/dx = -x/y and y(4) = 3; conic with A = C, B = 0 → circle.

steps.title: Sample space
steps.bodyLatex: $\{HH, HT, TH, TT\}$, all equally likely.

verification.note: SymPy: enumeration of the 4 outcomes gives 3/4.

jelet-2024-q030.conceptSummary: De Morgan: $A^{c}\cap B^{c} = (A\cup B)^{c}$ and $A^{c}\cup B^{c} = (A\cap B)^{c}$.

verification.note: SymPy: solving the addition rule gives P(A∩B) = 1/3, so P(A^c ∪ B^c) = 2/3.

jelet-2024-q031.conceptSummary: $B = I - A$ is also idempotent and annihilates $A$ from both sides. All four options are judged.

steps.title: (B) $AB = \theta$
steps.bodyLatex: $AB = A(I - A) = A - A^{2} = A - A = \theta$. TRUE.

steps.title: (C) $BA = \theta$
steps.bodyLatex: $BA = (I - A)A = A - A^{2} = \theta$. TRUE (even for non-symmetric idempotents such as $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$).

steps.title: (D)
steps.bodyLatex: Claims (C) is false, but (C) is true. FALSE.

verification.note: SymPy: non-commutative expansion with A^2 -> A gives B^2 - B = AB = BA = 0; also checked on a non-symmetric idempotent.

jelet-2024-q032.conceptSummary: If all three rows coincide at $x = a$, then $R_{2} - R_{1}$ and $R_{3} - R_{1}$ both vanish at $x = a$; each contributes a factor $(x - a)$. All four options are judged.

steps.title: Row operations
steps.bodyLatex: $\det A = \det\begin{pmatrix} R_{1} \\ R_{2} - R_{1} \\ R_{3} - R_{1} \end{pmatrix}$ (determinant unchanged).

steps.title: Factor theorem
steps.bodyLatex: Every entry of $R_{2} - R_{1}$ and of $R_{3} - R_{1}$ is a polynomial vanishing at $x = a$, so it is divisible by $(x - a)$. Taking $(x - a)$ out of each of these two rows gives $\det A = (x - a)^{2}\,Q(x)$.

steps.title: Judge the options
steps.bodyLatex: (A) TRUE (implied by (B)). (B) TRUE. (C) not always: e.g. rows $(1,0,0)$, $(1, x - a, 0)$, $(1, 0, x - a)$ coincide at $x = a$ and $\det A = (x - a)^{2}$ exactly. (D) FALSE.

verification.note: SymPy: for generic linear rows agreeing at x = a, det is divisible by (x-a)^2 but not (x-a)^3; explicit example det = (x-a)^2.

jelet-2024-q033.conceptSummary: Take moduli: $|i||Z|^{2} = |\overline Z| \Rightarrow |Z|^{2} = |Z|$. All four options are judged.

steps.title: Both values occur
steps.bodyLatex: $Z = 0$ works. For $|Z| = 1$ write $Z = e^{i\theta}$: $ie^{2i\theta} = e^{-i\theta} \iff e^{3i\theta} = -i$, e.g. $\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$ gives $Z = i$: $i\cdot i^{2} = -i = \overline{i}$. ✓

steps.title: Judge the options
steps.bodyLatex: (A) $0$: TRUE. (B) $1$: TRUE. (C) $2$ and (D) $3$ or $4$: FALSE, since $|Z|^{2} = |Z|$ admits only $0$ and $1$.

verification.note: SymPy: solving i(x+iy)^2 = x - iy over the reals gives 4 solutions with |Z| in {0, 1}.

jelet-2024-q034.conceptSummary: A hyperbola is rectangular iff its asymptotes are perpendicular, i.e. the $x^{2}$ and $y^{2}$ coefficients sum to zero. All four options are judged.

steps.title: (A) $xy = c^{2}$
steps.bodyLatex: Asymptotes are the axes $x = 0$, $y = 0$, which are perpendicular. TRUE.

steps.title: (B), (C)
steps.bodyLatex: Asymptotes $y = \pm\frac{b}{a}x$ (or $\pm\frac{a}{b}x$) are perpendicular only when $a = b$; for general $a \neq b$ the hyperbola is not rectangular. FALSE in general.

steps.title: (D) $x^{2} - y^{2} = c^{2}$
steps.bodyLatex: Asymptotes $y = \pm x$ are perpendicular ($a = b = c$). TRUE.

verification.note: SymPy: trace of the quadratic form = 0 and discriminant > 0 for A and D; for B, C trace = 1/a^2 - 1/b^2 ≠ 0 when a ≠ b.

jelet-2024-q035.conceptSummary: $[\vec a\times\vec b\;\;\vec b\times\vec c\;\;\vec c\times\vec a] = [\vec a\;\vec b\;\vec c]^{2}$. All four options are judged.

steps.title: Expand
steps.bodyLatex: $(\vec b\times\vec c)\times(\vec c\times\vec a) = [\vec b\;\vec c\;\vec a]\,\vec c$ (BAC–CAB with $\vec c\cdot(\vec c\times\vec a) = 0$).

steps.title: Dot with $\vec a\times\vec b$
steps.bodyLatex: $(\vec a\times\vec b)\cdot[\vec a\;\vec b\;\vec c]\,\vec c = [\vec a\;\vec b\;\vec c]\,[\vec a\;\vec b\;\vec c] = [\vec a\;\vec b\;\vec c]^{2}$.

steps.title: Judge the options
steps.bodyLatex: (C) TRUE. (D) coplanar $\Rightarrow [\vec a\;\vec b\;\vec c] = 0 \Rightarrow$ value $0$: TRUE. (A) $2[\vec a\;\vec b\;\vec c]$ and (B) $2[\vec a\;\vec b\;\vec c]^{2}$ differ from $[\vec a\;\vec b\;\vec c]^{2}$ whenever $[\vec a\;\vec b\;\vec c] \neq 0$ (e.g. $\hat i, \hat j, \hat k$: value $1$, not $2$). FALSE.

verification.note: SymPy: with symbolic 3-vectors, det[a×b, b×c, c×a] - det[a,b,c]^2 expands to 0.

jelet-2024-q036.conceptSummary: $f$ is piecewise linear with corners at $x = 1$ and $x = 2$. All four options are judged.

steps.title: Piecewise form
steps.bodyLatex: $f(x) = 3 - 2x$ for $x < 1$; $1$ for $1 \le x \le 2$; $2x - 3$ for $x > 2$. It is continuous on $\mathbb{R}$, since the pieces agree at $1$ and $2$.

steps.title: Derivability
steps.bodyLatex: At $x = 1$: $f'(1^{-}) = -2 \neq 0 = f'(1^{+})$. At $x = 2$: $f'(2^{-}) = 0 \neq 2 = f'(2^{+})$. Everywhere else $f$ is linear, hence derivable.

steps.title: Judge the options
steps.bodyLatex: (A) TRUE. (C) TRUE. (D) FALSE: $f$ is continuous everywhere. (B) is read, as in the official key, as \"not derivable (anywhere) in $\mathbb{R}$\", which is FALSE because $f$ is derivable at every $x \neq 1, 2$. Under the weaker reading \"not derivable on all of $\mathbb{R}$\" (B) would be true; the official key WBE/Ex-71 lists only (A), (C).

verification.note: SymPy: one-sided derivatives at 1 are (-2, 0) and at 2 are (0, 2); f is continuous at both. Interpretation note on (B) recorded.

jelet-2024-q037.conceptSummary: $f'(x) = 3(x^{2} - 4x + 8) = 3\big((x - 2)^{2} + 4\big) > 0$: strictly increasing, with no extremum. All four options are judged.

steps.title: Derivative
steps.bodyLatex: $f'(x) = 3x^{2} - 12x + 24$, with discriminant $144 - 288 = -144 < 0$, so $f'(x) > 0$ for every real $x$.

steps.title: Judge (A)–(C)
steps.bodyLatex: An extremum needs $f' = 0$, but $f'(2) = 12$, $f'(-1) = 39$, $f'(-2) = 60$. (A), (B), (C) are all FALSE.

steps.title: Judge (D)
steps.bodyLatex: $f$ is strictly increasing on $\mathbb{R}$, so it has neither a maximum nor a minimum. TRUE.

verification.note: SymPy: discriminant of f' = -144 < 0; solve(f' = 0) has no real roots.

jelet-2024-q038.conceptSummary: Over $[-\pi, \pi]$, odd parts integrate to zero. All four options are judged.

steps.title: Judge the options
steps.bodyLatex: (C) only $c$: TRUE. (A) only $a$, (B) only $b$: FALSE. (D) \"only $a, c$\": FALSE, because the value does not depend on $a$ either.

verification.note: SymPy: integral = 2*pi^3*c/3; partial derivatives with respect to a and b are 0.

jelet-2024-q039.conceptSummary: $y'' + y = 0$ has general solution $y = C_{1}\cos x + C_{2}\sin x$; every linear combination is a solution. All four options are judged.

steps.title: Characteristic equation
steps.bodyLatex: $m^{2} + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow m = \pm i$, so $y = C_{1}\cos x + C_{2}\sin x$.

verification.note: SymPy: diff(y, x, 2) + y simplifies to 0 for all four option functions.

jelet-2024-q040.conceptSummary: Independence: $P(A'\cap B) = (1 - p)q$ and $P(A\cap B') = p(1 - q)$ with $p = P(A)$, $q = P(B)$. All four options are judged.

steps.title: Judge the options
steps.bodyLatex: (B) $\frac16$ and (C) $\frac45$ are possible values of $P(B)$: TRUE. (A) $\frac15$ and (D) $\frac56$ are values of $P(A)$, not $P(B)$: FALSE.

jelet-2024-q041.conceptSummary: Write $[M] = [F]^{a}[T]^{b}[V]^{c}$ and match the exponents of the SI base dimensions.

steps.title: Match with $[M] = M^{1}L^{0}T^{0}$
steps.bodyLatex: $M$: $a = 1$. $L$: $a + c = 0 \Rightarrow c = -1$. $T$: $-2a + b - c = 0 \Rightarrow b = 2a + c = 1$.

steps.title: Physical check
steps.bodyLatex: $m = F/a_{acc} = F\,t/v$, so $[M] = FTV^{-1}$. (A) $FT^{2}V^{-2}$ has dimension $ML^{-1}T^{2}$, not mass.

verification.note: SymPy: solve exponent system -> (a, b, c) = (1, 1, -1).

jelet-2024-q042.conceptSummary: In projectile motion $a_x = 0$ and $a_y = -g$: $v_x$ is constant, while the speed $|v_y| = |u\sin\theta - gt|$ falls linearly to $0$ at the top and then rises linearly.

steps.title: Horizontal component
steps.bodyLatex: No horizontal force, so $v_x = u\cos\theta$ for all $t$: a horizontal line on the $v_x$–$t$ graph.

steps.title: Vertical component
steps.bodyLatex: $v_y = u\sin\theta - gt$. The speed along $y$ is $|v_y|$: it decreases linearly with slope $-g$ to $0$ at $t = u\sin\theta/g$ (the highest point), then increases linearly with slope $+g$, a V shape.

steps.title: Match the graphs
steps.bodyLatex: (A): $v_x$ constant and $v_y$ a V shape, matching. (B) swaps the components. (C) has $|v_y|$ starting from $0$, but at launch $|v_y| = u\sin\theta \neq 0$. (D) has $v_x$ varying.

verification.note: SVG: panel shapes read back from fig-2024-q42-opt*.svg; only (A) has (constant, V-shape).

jelet-2024-q043.conceptSummary: The frequency is unchanged at refraction, so $\lambda \propto v \propto 1/n$. In the figure both $\alpha_{1}$ and $\alpha_{2}$ are measured from the normal, so Snell's law applies directly.

steps.title: Read the angles
steps.bodyLatex: In the figure the arc $\alpha_{1}$ runs from the normal (vertical line) to the incident ray in medium 1, and $\alpha_{2}$ from the normal to the refracted ray in medium 2. Both are angles with the normal.

steps.title: Wavelength
steps.bodyLatex: $f$ is fixed and $v = c/n$, so $\lambda = v/f \propto 1/n$ and $\dfrac{\lambda_{2}}{\lambda_{1}} = \dfrac{n_{1}}{n_{2}} = \dfrac{\sin\alpha_{2}}{\sin\alpha_{1}}$. Here $\alpha_{2} > \alpha_{1}$ (the ray bends away from the normal), so medium 2 is optically rarer and $\lambda_{2} > \lambda_{1}$.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: $\lambda_{2} = \dfrac{\sin\alpha_{2}}{\sin\alpha_{1}}\lambda_{1}$. Answer: (B). (D) would follow only if the angles were measured from the interface.

verification.note: SVG: arcs alpha1/alpha2 start on the normal and end on the incident/refracted rays; drawn angles 35 deg / 54 deg; Snell ratio sin(a2)/sin(a1) = n1/n2.

steps.title: Stress
steps.bodyLatex: $\sigma = \dfrac{12.4\pi}{4\pi\times10^{-6}} = 3.1\times10^{6}\,\text{Nm}^{-2}$. The $\pi$ cancels, which is why $g$ was given as $3.1\pi$.

jelet-2024-q045.conceptSummary: $\vec{L} = m\,\vec{r}\times\vec{v}$ depends on the reference point. About $C$, $L_c = mvR$; about the point $O$ on the circle it is $mvR(1 + \cos\theta)$.

steps.title: Coordinates
steps.bodyLatex: Put $C$ at the origin and $O = (-R, 0)$, the left end of the diameter. The particle is at $P = R(\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$, moving counter-clockwise with $\vec{v} = v(-\sin\theta, \cos\theta)$.

steps.title: About $O$
steps.bodyLatex: $\vec{r}_{OP} = (R(1 + \cos\theta),\, R\sin\theta)$. $(\vec{r}_{OP}\times\vec{v})_z = R(1 + \cos\theta)\,v\cos\theta - R\sin\theta\,(-v\sin\theta) = Rv(1 + \cos\theta)$. So $L_o = mvR(1 + \cos\theta)$.

steps.title: Ratio
steps.bodyLatex: $\dfrac{L_o}{L_c} = 1 + \cos\theta$. Note $1 + \cos\theta = 2\cos^{2}\dfrac{\theta}{2}$, so (C) is off by a factor of 2. Answer: (B).

verification.note: SymPy: cross products give L_O/L_C = 1 + cos(theta) identically; SVG: O on circle at the left end of the diameter, numeric ratio from drawn geometry matches.

jelet-2024-q046.conceptSummary: Starting from rest, $v(t) = \int_0^t a\,dt$. Since $a \geq 0$ until $t = 25\,\text{s}$, $v$ is maximum there and equals the area under the $a$–$t$ graph.

steps.title: Acceleration law
steps.bodyLatex: From the graph $a(t) = 10\left(1 - \dfrac{t}{25}\right)\,\text{ms}^{-2}$ for $0 \leq t \leq 25\,\text{s}$, and $a = 0$ afterwards.

steps.title: Velocity
steps.bodyLatex: $v(t) = \int_0^t a\,dt = 10t - \dfrac{t^{2}}{5}$. $\dfrac{dv}{dt} = a = 0$ at $t = 25\,\text{s}$, and $a > 0$ before that, so this is the maximum.

steps.title: Area
steps.bodyLatex: $v_{max} = v(25) = 250 - 125 = 125\,\text{ms}^{-1}$, which equals the triangle area $\tfrac12 \times 25 \times 10$.

verification.note: SVG: a-t line read back from fig-2024-q46.svg with tick labels 10 and 25 -> area = 125.

jelet-2024-q047.conceptSummary: Only $80\%$ of the power heats the block: $0.8\,P\,t = M s\,\Delta T$.

steps.title: Energy available
steps.bodyLatex: In time $t$ the machine delivers $Pt$. $20\%$ is lost to heating the machine, so $0.8\,Pt$ goes into the block.

steps.title: Solve
steps.bodyLatex: $\Delta T = \dfrac{0.8\,Pt}{Ms}$. (D) uses the lost $20\%$ instead, and (C) is dimensionally wrong (it has $1/t$).

verification.note: SymPy: solve(0.8*P*t - M*s*dT, dT) = 0.8*P*t/(M*s).

jelet-2024-q048.conceptSummary: Apparent expansion $=$ real expansion of the liquid $-$ cubical expansion of the vessel: $\gamma^{a} = \gamma_{r} - 3\alpha$.

steps.title: Relation
steps.bodyLatex: The vessel's volume grows with $\gamma_{v} = 3\alpha$, so the liquid appears to expand by $\gamma^{a} = \gamma_{r} - 3\alpha_{vessel}$.

steps.title: Same liquid
steps.bodyLatex: $\gamma_{r}$ is the same in both vessels: $\gamma_{A}^{a} = \gamma_{r} - 3\alpha_{A}$ and $\gamma_{B}^{a} = \gamma_{r} - 3\alpha_{B}$.

verification.note: SymPy: (g - 3aA) - (g - 3aB) = -3(aA - aB) < 0 for aA > aB.

jelet-2024-q049.conceptSummary: Two slabs in series add their thermal resistances $R = \dfrac{L}{kA}$. The correct steady heat current, $\dfrac{kA(t_{1} - t_{2})}{2l}$, is not among the options, so WBJEEB withdrew the item.

steps.title: Thermal resistances
steps.bodyLatex: Part 1: $R_{1} = \dfrac{l}{kA}$. Part 2: $R_{2} = \dfrac{2l}{(2k)A} = \dfrac{l}{kA}$. In series: $R = R_{1} + R_{2} = \dfrac{2l}{kA}$.

steps.title: Heat current
steps.bodyLatex: $H = \dfrac{t_{1} - t_{2}}{R} = \dfrac{kA(t_{1} - t_{2})}{2l}$. Junction check: $t_{J} = \dfrac{t_{1} + t_{2}}{2}$, and each part carries $kA\,\dfrac{t_{1} - t_{J}}{l} = \dfrac{kA(t_{1} - t_{2})}{2l}$.

steps.title: Compare with the options
steps.bodyLatex: (A) $\dfrac{3kA(t_{2} - t_{1})}{2l}$ is negative and $3\times$ too large. (B) is $4\times$, (C) $2\times$ and (D) $\tfrac{2}{3}\times$ the correct value. None equals $\dfrac{kA(t_{1} - t_{2})}{2l}$.

steps.title: Why the item was withdrawn
steps.bodyLatex: No option is correct, so the single-correct question has no valid answer. The WBJEEB final key WBE/Ex-71 marks Q49 W (withdrawn).

steps.title: Marking
steps.bodyLatex: Q49 is a Category-I item marked W (withdrawn). It awards the full $+1$ mark ($+12$ twelfths) to every candidate, whatever they marked.

verification.note: SymPy: H = kA(t1-t2)/(2l); ratios of options to H = -3, 4, 2, 2/3 -> no option correct -> W, +1 mark (+12 twelfths) to all.

jelet-2024-q050.conceptSummary: A hypermetropic eye has its near point $D$ beyond $25\,\text{cm}$. The convex lens must image an object at $25\,\text{cm}$ at the near point $D$, on the same side as the object.

steps.title: Near point
steps.bodyLatex: $v = -40\,\text{cm}$: a virtual image $40\,\text{cm}$ in front of the eye, which is where the defective eye can just see clearly.

jelet-2024-q051.conceptSummary: Thermal conductivity $k$ is defined by $H = kA\,\dfrac{\Delta T}{L}$. It is a material constant.

steps.title: Definition
steps.bodyLatex: Fourier's law: $H = kA\,\dfrac{\Delta T}{L}$. The heat current $H$ depends on $A$, $L$ and $\Delta T$, but $k = \dfrac{HL}{A\,\Delta T}$ removes this geometric dependence.

steps.title: What remains
steps.bodyLatex: $k$ depends only on the material (and its temperature), not on length, mass or cross-section. Those quantities fix the thermal resistance $L/(kA)$, not $k$ itself.

verification.note: SymPy: k = H*L/(A*dT) is invariant under scaling L, A (H scales as A/L).

jelet-2024-q052.conceptSummary: The vertical cut halves the lens into two plano-convex halves of focal length $2f$, and the horizontal cut does not change the focal length. The four plano-convex quarter pieces are then placed in contact along the axis, so their powers add.

steps.title: Each piece
steps.bodyLatex: For the equiconvex lens, $\dfrac{1}{f} = (\mu - 1)\dfrac{2}{R}$. Each quarter has one curved face (radius $R$) and one flat face, so $\dfrac{1}{f_{piece}} = (\mu - 1)\dfrac{1}{R} = \dfrac{1}{2f}$. (The horizontal cut only reduces the aperture.)

steps.title: Arrangement
steps.bodyLatex: In the figure all four pieces A, B, C, D stand side by side along the same line, so light passes through them one after another. Thin lenses in contact add their powers.

verification.note: SymPy: 1/F = 4*(mu-1)/R with 1/f = 2(mu-1)/R -> F = f/2; SVG: four pieces, each with exactly one curved face.

jelet-2024-q053.conceptSummary: The first law, $\Delta Q = \Delta U + \Delta W$, is the law of conservation of energy applied to thermodynamic systems.

steps.title: Statement
steps.bodyLatex: Heat supplied to a system $=$ increase in internal energy $+$ work done by the system: $\delta Q = dU + \delta W$.

steps.title: Interpretation
steps.bodyLatex: Heat and work are two modes of energy transfer, and the energy balance is exact: energy is neither created nor destroyed. Heat alone is not conserved (it converts to work), and the law says nothing about momentum.

verification.note: SymPy: dU = dQ - dW, a closed energy balance (sum of transfers = change of internal energy).

jelet-2024-q054.conceptSummary: Each side carries $5 + 10 = 15\,\text{kg}$, so the system is balanced ($a = 0$) and every string tension equals the weight hanging below it.

steps.title: Acceleration
steps.bodyLatex: Left: $5 + 10 = 15\,\text{kg}$; right: $10 + 5 = 15\,\text{kg}$. Equal masses over a frictionless pulley give $a = 0$, so the system is at rest or moves uniformly.

steps.title: Tensions
steps.bodyLatex: $T_{1}$ supports $15\,\text{kg}$: $T_{1} = 15g$. $T_{2}$ (left, lower string) supports the lower $10\,\text{kg}$: $T_{2} = 10g$. $T_{3}$ (right, lower string) supports the lower $5\,\text{kg}$: $T_{3} = 5g$.

verification.note: SVG: block masses and sides read from fig-2024-q54.svg; SymPy: a = 0, (T1, T2, T3) = (15g, 10g, 5g).

jelet-2024-q055.conceptSummary: Einstein's equation $eV_o = h\nu - \phi$ gives a straight line $V_o = \dfrac{h}{e}\nu - \dfrac{\phi}{e}$, whose intercept on the $V_o$-axis is $-\phi/e$.

steps.title: Linear relation
steps.bodyLatex: $V_o = \dfrac{h}{e}\nu - \dfrac{\phi}{e}$: the slope (line $AC$) is $h/e$, and at $\nu = 0$ the extended line meets the $V_o$-axis at $A$, where $V_o = -\phi/e$.

steps.title: Read the figure
steps.bodyLatex: $A$ lies on the $V_o$-axis below $O$, so $OA = \phi/e$ (in volts). $B$ is the threshold frequency $\nu_{0} = \phi/h$.

steps.title: Work function
steps.bodyLatex: $\phi = e \times OA$, the product of the intercept $OA$ and the electronic charge. (A) slope $= h/e$; (B) $e \times$ slope $= h$; (D) $OA = \phi/e$ is a potential, not an energy.

verification.note: SVG: A on the V_o axis below O, B on the nu axis, A-B-C collinear; SymPy: intercept = -phi/e -> phi = e*OA.

jelet-2024-q056.conceptSummary: A small extra depression $y$ adds a buoyant restoring force $\sigma g A y$, giving SHM with $\omega^{2} = \dfrac{\sigma g A}{m}$ and $m = \rho A H$.

steps.title: Equilibrium
steps.bodyLatex: Floating: $\rho A H g = \sigma A h_{0} g$, where $h_{0}$ is the submerged depth.

steps.title: Restoring force
steps.bodyLatex: Push down by $y$: extra buoyancy $\sigma A g\,y$ upward, so $m\ddot{y} = -\sigma A g\,y$ with $m = \rho A H$.

steps.title: Angular frequency
steps.bodyLatex: $\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{\sigma A g}{\rho A H}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{\sigma g}{\rho H}}$, independent of the radius $R$ (the area cancels).

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A). The stem says frequency, but every option is written as $\omega$, the angular frequency.

verification.note: SymPy: m*y'' = -sigma*A*g*y with m = rho*A*H -> omega^2 = sigma*g/(rho*H).

jelet-2024-q057.conceptSummary: Equilibrium points are where $F = -\dfrac{dV}{dx} = 0$, i.e. the turning points of $V(x)$. A maximum is unstable and a minimum is stable.

steps.title: Turning points
steps.bodyLatex: The curve rises to a maximum, falls to a minimum, rises to a second (lower) maximum, then falls. That gives three points with $dV/dx = 0$. The end-points of the drawn curve are not turning points.

steps.title: Stability
steps.bodyLatex: At a maximum $d^{2}V/dx^{2} < 0$: a small displacement gives a force away from the point (unstable). At a minimum $d^{2}V/dx^{2} > 0$: restoring (stable).

steps.title: Count
steps.bodyLatex: Two maxima give two unstable points; one minimum gives one stable point.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Three equilibrium points, one stable and two unstable. Answer: (C).

verification.note: SVG: polyline of fig-2024-q57.svg has extrema (max, min, max) -> 1 stable, 2 unstable.

jelet-2024-q058.conceptSummary: Above the surface $g_h = g\left(\dfrac{R}{R + h}\right)^{2}$. A $2\%$ decrease gives $h \approx 64\,\text{km}$ with the binomial approximation, and $h = 64.98\,\text{km}$ exactly; neither matches an option, so WBJEEB withdrew the item.

steps.title: Approximate formula
steps.bodyLatex: $g_h \approx g\left(1 - \dfrac{2h}{R}\right)$. $\dfrac{\Delta g}{g} = \dfrac{2h}{R} = 0.02 \Rightarrow h = 0.01R = 64\,\text{km}$, which is not among the options.

steps.title: Exact formula
steps.bodyLatex: $\left(\dfrac{R}{R + h}\right)^{2} = 0.98 \Rightarrow h = R\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{0.98}} - 1\right) = 6400 \times 0.0101525 = 64.98\,\text{km}$, also not among the options (the nearest, $65.3\,\text{km}$, is off by $0.3\,\text{km}$). Going below the surface, $g(1 - d/R) = 0.98g$ gives $d = 128\,\text{km}$; a height can only decrease $g$.

steps.title: Why the item was withdrawn
steps.bodyLatex: Options (A) $62.5$, (B) $63.9$, (C) $64.2$, (D) $65.3\,\text{km}$: none equals $64\,\text{km}$ or $64.98\,\text{km}$, and “approximately” does not single one out. The WBJEEB final key WBE/Ex-71 marks Q58 W (withdrawn).

steps.title: Marking
steps.bodyLatex: Q58 is a Category-I item marked W (withdrawn). It awards the full $+1$ mark ($+12$ twelfths) to every candidate, whatever they marked.

verification.note: SymPy: h_approx = 64 km, h_exact = 6400*(1/sqrt(0.98) - 1) = 64.976 km; no option equals either -> W, +1 mark (+12 twelfths) to all.

jelet-2024-q059.conceptSummary: Kepler's third law gives $r_{2} = 4\times10^{4}\,\text{km}$. At closest approach both velocities are parallel, so the angular speed seen from $S_{1}$ is $\dfrac{|v_{2} - v_{1}|}{r_{2} - r_{1}}$.

steps.title: Relative motion at closest approach
steps.bodyLatex: Both satellites are on the same radial line and move in the same sense: relative velocity $|v_{2} - v_{1}| = \pi\times10^{4}\,\text{km/h}$, perpendicular to the separation $r_{2} - r_{1} = 3\times10^{4}\,\text{km}$.

jelet-2024-q060.conceptSummary: Standing, the rain's velocity relative to the ground makes $30^{\circ}$ with the vertical. Running at $10\,\text{km/h}$ removes the horizontal component, leaving only the vertical part.

steps.title: Components
steps.bodyLatex: $\vec{V}_{rg} = (V_{rg}\sin30^{\circ},\, -V_{rg}\cos30^{\circ})$, with the horizontal part along the man's running direction.

verification.note: SymPy: solve(Vrg*sin(30deg) - 10) -> 20; Vrm = 20*cos(30deg) = 10*sqrt(3).

jelet-2024-q061.conceptSummary: $V = mgH - \tfrac12 mg^{2}t^{2}$ and $K = \tfrac12 mg^{2}t^{2}$. Both are parabolas in $t$ with zero slope at $t = 0$, their sum stays $mgH$, and they end at $t = \sqrt{2H/g}$.

steps.title: Kinematics
steps.bodyLatex: From rest: $y$ fallen $= \tfrac12 gt^{2}$, $v = gt$. The particle lands when $\tfrac12 gT^{2} = H$, i.e. $T = \sqrt{2H/g}$.

steps.title: Energies
steps.bodyLatex: $K = \tfrac12 m(gt)^{2} = \tfrac12 mg^{2}t^{2}$, concave up and starting flat. $V = mg\left(H - \tfrac12 gt^{2}\right)$, concave down and starting flat at $mgH$. $V + K = mgH$ at every instant.

steps.title: Compare the graphs
steps.bodyLatex: (A): V concave down from $mgH$, K concave up from $0$, crossing at $V = K = mgH/2$ and ending at $\sqrt{2h/g}$, all correct. (B): K is concave down (it rises steeply at $t = 0$, but $\dot K = mg^{2}t = 0$ there). (C): V is concave up (steep at $t = 0$, but $\dot V = 0$ there). (D): the curve shapes are right but the end time $\sqrt{h/g}$ is wrong.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A). (The graphs print a lower-case $h$ for the height $H$ of the stem.)

verification.note: SVG: V/K polylines read back from fig-2024-q61-opt*.svg; only (A) has V concave-down, K concave-up, V+K const and end label sqrt(2h/g).

jelet-2024-q062.conceptSummary: Substitute $t = 2\,\text{s}$ into $X(t)$ and $Y(t)$ with the given constants.

jelet-2024-q063.conceptSummary: Use $U = -\dfrac{GMm}{r}$ with $GM = g_{o}R^{2}$. The change from $r = R$ to $r = 2R$ is $\dfrac{mg_{o}R}{2}$.

steps.title: Use $g_{o}$
steps.bodyLatex: $g_{o} = \dfrac{GM}{R^{2}} \Rightarrow GM = g_{o}R^{2}$, so $\Delta U = \dfrac{mg_{o}R}{2}$. It is positive (work is done against gravity). $mg_{o}R$ (A) would wrongly assume constant $g$ up to height $R$.

verification.note: SymPy: G*M*m*(1/R - 1/(2R)) with G*M = g0*R^2 -> m*g0*R/2.

jelet-2024-q064.conceptSummary: For small oscillations $T = 2\pi\sqrt{l/g}$, which does not depend on the bob's mass.

steps.title: Equation of motion
steps.bodyLatex: $m l\ddot{\theta} = -mg\sin\theta \approx -mg\theta$. The mass cancels on both sides.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Doubling the mass leaves $T$ unchanged. Answer: (D).

verification.note: SymPy: m*l*th'' = -m*g*th -> omega^2 = g/l, independent of m.

jelet-2024-q065.conceptSummary: The graph is a parabola $V = V_{o} + \tfrac12 kx^{2}$ with its minimum on the $V$-axis, so $F = -\dfrac{dV}{dx} = -kx$.

steps.title: Shape
steps.bodyLatex: The curve is symmetric about the $V$-axis with its lowest point $V_{o}$ at $x = 0$: $V(x) = V_{o} + \tfrac12 kx^{2}$, $k > 0$.

steps.title: Force
steps.bodyLatex: $F = -\dfrac{dV}{dx} = -kx$. The constant $V_{o}$ only shifts the energy zero and drops out on differentiation.

steps.title: Reject the others
steps.bodyLatex: (B) would need a maximum at $x = 0$. (C) $-kx^{2}$ corresponds to a cubic $V$. (D) $F_{o} \neq 0$ would put the minimum at $x = F_{o}/k \neq 0$, off the $V$-axis, contrary to the figure.

verification.note: SVG: quadratic fit of fig-2024-q65.svg has its vertex on the V-axis (F0 = 0); SymPy: -d/dx(V0 + k x^2/2) = -k x.

jelet-2024-q066.conceptSummary: With $F = -bv$, write $a = v\dfrac{dv}{dx}$: then $mv\dfrac{dv}{dx} = -bv \Rightarrow \dfrac{dv}{dx} = -\dfrac{b}{m}$, so $V$ falls linearly with $x$.

steps.title: Integrate
steps.bodyLatex: $V(x) = V_{o} - \dfrac{b}{m}x$: a straight line that reaches $V = 0$ at the finite distance $x_{max} = \dfrac{mV_{o}}{b}$. (In time, $v = V_{o}e^{-bt/m}$ decays exponentially, and $x(t) = \dfrac{mV_{o}}{b}(1 - e^{-bt/m}) \to x_{max}$.)

steps.title: Judge each graph
steps.bodyLatex: (A) and (C) are exponential-type curves: these are $v$–$t$ shapes, not $v$–$x$ (false). (B) is a straight line from $V_{o}$ to $0$ at finite $x$ (true). (D) oscillates about $V = 0$, but the velocity never reverses under a pure drag force (false).

verification.note: SymPy: dsolve(m*v*v' + b*v) -> V = V0 - b x/m; SVG: only option (B) polyline is straight (max deviation 0) and reaches V = 0; true set {B}.

jelet-2024-q067.conceptSummary: In the plate's frame the normal reaction is $N = ma$. Friction must hold the weight: $\mu N \geq mg$, so $\mu \geq \dfrac{g}{a}$.

steps.title: Forces
steps.bodyLatex: The plate pushes the block horizontally with $N = ma$ (this is what accelerates the block with the plate). Vertically, static friction $f$ balances the weight: $f = mg$.

steps.title: Friction limit
steps.bodyLatex: $f \leq \mu N \Rightarrow mg \leq \mu ma \Rightarrow \mu \geq \dfrac{g}{a}$ (here $m = 1\,\text{kg}$, but the mass cancels anyway).

steps.title: Judge each option
steps.bodyLatex: (A) $\mu < g/a$: the block slides down (false). (B) $\mu > g/a$: held, friction not limiting (true). (C) $\mu = g/a$: held, friction limiting (true). (D) $\mu = a/g$ satisfies $\mu \geq g/a$ only when $a \geq g$, so it is not a valid general statement (false).

verification.note: SymPy: condition mu >= g/a; truth set over a in (0, inf): A False, B True, C True, D False (fails for a < g) -> {B, C}.

jelet-2024-q068.conceptSummary: Same material, so the thermal resistance is $R = L/(kA)$. Rod C has twice the length and twice the area of A, so $R_{C} = R_{A} = R_{B}$. Then $\sum H = 0$ at the junction.

verification.note: SymPy: solve(T + (T-100) + (T-100), T) = 200/3; SVG: rod C drawn wider than A and B.

jelet-2024-q069.conceptSummary: Volume is conserved: $8 \cdot \tfrac43\pi r^{3} = \tfrac43\pi R^{3} \Rightarrow R = 2r$. The surface energy is proportional to the area.

steps.title: Areas
steps.bodyLatex: Initial: $8 \times 4\pi r^{2} = 32\pi r^{2}$. Final: $4\pi R^{2} = 16\pi r^{2}$.

steps.title: Ratio
steps.bodyLatex: $E_{f} : E_{i} = 16 : 32 = 1 : 2$ (the same surface tension $T$ multiplies both).

jelet-2024-q070.conceptSummary: For an adiabat $PV^{\gamma} = $ const, so $\dfrac{dP}{dV} = -\gamma\dfrac{P}{V}$. From a common state, the steeper curve has the larger $\gamma$.

steps.title: Read the figure
steps.bodyLatex: Both curves start from the same point $(P, V)$, and gas 1 falls more steeply than gas 2. So $\gamma_{1} > \gamma_{2}$.

steps.title: Values of $\gamma$
steps.bodyLatex: Monatomic He, Ar: $\gamma = \tfrac53$. Diatomic N$_{2}$, O$_{2}$: $\gamma = \tfrac75$. CO$_{2}$ (polyatomic): $\gamma \approx 1.3$. Pairs (gas 1, gas 2): (A) He, N$_{2}$: $\tfrac53 > \tfrac75$ (true). (B) N$_{2}$, He (false). (C) CO$_{2}$, O$_{2}$: $1.3 < 1.4$ (false). (D) CO$_{2}$, Ar: $1.3 < 1.67$ (false).

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.bodyLatex: Answer: (A) He and N$_{2}$ (the only correct option).

verification.note: SVG: initial slopes of gas1/gas2 polylines from the common start -> |slope1| > |slope2| -> gamma1 > gamma2; only pair (A) satisfies it.

Doping.

steps.bodyLatex: N from +2 and +4 both go to +4 — comproportionation.

verification.note: Key C.

jelet-2024-q077.conceptSummary: Le Chatelier's principle and volume change.

steps.title: Analyze
steps.bodyLatex: Decrease in volume favors fewer gas moles.

steps.title: Check options
steps.bodyLatex: Only (C) has fewer gas moles on product side.

verification.note: Le Chatelier.

steps.title: Analyze
steps.bodyLatex: $Na_2CO_3$ is salt of strong base + weak acid → basic.

verification.note: Salt hydrolysis.

steps.title: Analysis
